title: Safety and immunogenicity of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine administered to adults: A phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in adults who had previously completed a primary vaccination series with or without a booster, addressing the need for improved vaccine strategies against emerging variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial was conducted among healthy adults aged ≥18 years who had completed a primary COVID-19 mRNA vaccination series, with or without a booster, at least 3 months prior.
analysis.methods: Participants were randomized in a 1:1:1:1:1 ratio to receive either an investigational bivalent mRNA vaccine encoding ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 spike proteins, an investigational monovalent mRNA vaccine encoding Omicron BA.4-5 spike protein, or a licensed Original Wuhan/Omicron BA.4-5 bivalent mRNA vaccine.
analysis.main_results: At Day 8, CD4+ T cells (Th1 profile) increased in all study groups, while CD8+ T cells increased in all groups except the lowest CV0701 dose group. No vaccine-related serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases were reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that the investigational vaccines elicited robust humoral and cellular immunity with an acceptable safety profile, comparable to a licensed bivalent mRNA vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide cautious support for the use of these investigational vaccines in boosting immunity against SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly in adults with prior vaccination histories.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to healthy adults and did not include long-term follow-up, but the evidence is strong due to the randomized, controlled design and the inclusion of multiple vaccine types.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of two investigational mRNA vaccines (CV0701 and CV0601) encoding SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins, compared to a licensed bivalent vaccine, in adults who had completed a primary vaccination series with or without a booster. The study found that all vaccines elicited robust immune responses, with no serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases reported. CD4+ T cells increased in all groups, while CD8+ T cells increased in all groups except the lowest CV0701 dose group. The results suggest that these vaccines are safe and immunogenic, comparable to the licensed vaccine. However, the study was limited to healthy adults and lacked long-term follow-up, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong due to the controlled design and comprehensive immune response evaluation.

title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in 70.2% (33/47) of immunocompromised patients with mAb-resistant infections, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term outcomes, durability of viral clearance, or comparative efficacy against newer antiviral agents. Additionally, the small sample size (47 cases) and reliance on unpublished cases limit generalizability and robustness of conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for randomized controlled trials to validate CCP efficacy in immunocompromised populations and to determine optimal dosing strategies. Surveillance for emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants resistant to both mAbs and CCP is recommended to guide treatment protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes correlating with improved outcomes. The review underscores CCP's potential role in overcoming mAb resistance but emphasizes the need for larger, controlled studies to confirm efficacy, optimize dosing, and assess long-term durability. Given the limited sample size and reliance on unpublished data, findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Immunological effects of supervised exercise in long COVID in adults: A secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial

analysis.research_question_and_background: Long COVID (post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection) affects approximately 5%–30% of survivors and is characterized by persistent fatigue, dyspnea, exercise intolerance, and cognitive impairment. We evaluated the immunological effects of supervised exercise in adults with long COVID.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this pre‐specified exploratory substudy of the EXER‐COVID randomized 2 × 2 crossover trial, participants completed a 6‐week supervised exercise program (twice weekly) or usual care before crossing over after a 3–5 day washout. Immunophenotyping included 20 CD4 + and CD8 + T‐cell subsets and five innate immune populations.
analysis.methods: Plasma cytokines (IL‐1β, IL‐6, IL‐10, TNF‐α, MCP‐1/CCL2, MIP‐1α/CCL3, MIP‐1β/CCL4, and IP‐10/CXCL10) were measured by multiplex immunoassay. Treatment effects were estimated using within‐period change scores, with multiple testing controlled by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure (false discovery rate < 5%).
analysis.main_results: Five variables reached nominal significance before correction (two CD8 + T‐cell subsets and IL‐1β, IL‐10, and MIP‐1α), but none remained significant after adjustment. No changes were observed in innate immune populations, and no evidence of carryover was detected.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Supervised exercise was not associated with significant immunological changes after correction for multiple comparisons, supporting the short‐term immunological safety of moderate‐intensity exercise in PESE‐negative adults with long COVID.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that supervised exercise may be a safe intervention for adults with long COVID, potentially informing future studies on therapeutic approaches for this condition.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial, and the results were adjusted for multiple comparisons. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the exploratory nature of the analysis and the potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunological effects of supervised exercise in adults with long COVID, a condition affecting 5%–30% of SARS-CoV-2 survivors. It was a secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial where participants underwent a 6-week supervised exercise program or usual care, followed by a washout period. Plasma cytokines and immunophenotyping were measured using multiplex immunoassays. Despite five variables showing nominal significance before correction, none remained significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. No changes were observed in innate immune populations, and no carryover effects were detected. The results support the short-term immunological safety of moderate-intensity exercise in adults with long COVID. The study's findings are of moderate evidence strength due to its exploratory nature and the potential for confounding factors. The results may inform future research on therapeutic interventions for long COVID but do not provide definitive conclusions.

title: Psychoeducational Challenges of Dyslexic Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review.

The central question is about the impact of the pandemic on dyslexic children's learning and mental health.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that dyslexic children experienced significant psychological and educational challenges during the pandemic. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to support these children in the post-pandemic period.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the evidence is limited in scope, with a focus on psychological and educational challenges rather than biological or virological aspects of SARS-CoV-2. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The research suggests that targeted, evidence-based strategies are needed to mitigate the challenges faced by dyslexic children during and after the pandemic. The review emphasizes the importance of these interventions for improving educational outcomes and mental health for dyslexic children.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the psychoeducational challenges experienced by dyslexic children during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in the context of online learning. The review highlights the importance of targeted interventions, such as teacher training, family-school collaboration, adaptive learning technologies, and psychological support, to address these challenges. The evidence base includes articles retrieved from PubMed, Wiley, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, with additional references gathered through snowballing. While the findings are consistent across the included studies, the review notes limitations in the scope of evidence, particularly regarding the biological or virological aspects of SARS-CoV-2 and the long-term implications of the identified challenges.

title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) for COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2, focusing on three interacting determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics, to reconcile conflicting trial outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM) was conducted, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through May 2026, applying a standardized 91-field extraction matrix to 31 included studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CP is effective only under specific conditions: early administration, sufficient antibody titre, and in seronegative or immunocompromised hosts lacking endogenous antibody responses. Among RCTs, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration, 3 of 4 with higher-titre CP, and two large RCTs (n=12,522) showed preferential benefit in seronegative recipients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM) in CP products is nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies reporting such data despite evidence of their potent neutralising activity against SARS-CoV-2, representing a systematic gap in product assessment.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritise standardised quantification of IgA/IgM titres in CP products and evaluate precision deployment strategies for passive immunotherapy in future pandemics, leveraging timing and titre determinants to optimise efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review resolves conflicting evidence on convalescent plasma (CP) efficacy in COVID-19 by identifying three critical determinants: early administration, high antibody titre, and host seronegativity or immunocompromise. Among 31 studies (20,793 patients), randomized trials showed benefit when CP was given early (4/6 trials) or with higher titres (3/4 trials), particularly in seronegative recipients (two large RCTs, n=12,522). However, a major evidence gap persists: only 2 studies assessed non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM), despite their potential potency. The review reframes CP efficacy as conditional and provides a template for precision deployment in future pandemics, emphasizing the need for standardized IgA/IgM quantification and targeted clinical strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the incomplete understanding of mechanisms driving the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events in COVID-19, aiming to identify novel prothrombotic alterations associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An exploratory, integrated analysis was conducted on cerebral thrombi retrieved by mechanical thrombectomy from six stroke patients with COVID-19 and six without COVID-19 during the first pandemic wave.
analysis.methods: Histological and ultrastructural assessments were combined with quantitative proteomics (LC–MS/MS) and elemental profiling (TXRF) to compare cellular organization, protein composition, and metal content between thrombi from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients.
analysis.main_results: COVID-19 thrombi showed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance and diffuse CD68+ staining, reduced platelet content, and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase, and redox-regulating proteins, and downregulation of platelet-related proteins. TXRF confirmed increased iron levels, while glycophorin A immunostaining and erythrocyte structural proteins indicated cell-free hemoglobin and iron presence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as supporting a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability involving elevated cell-free hemoglobin and iron, distinct from NETs burden or erythrocyte abundance. They highlight the identification of hemoglobin/iron-related processes as a potential molecular target for future therapies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that hemoglobin and iron dysregulation may contribute to the prothrombotic state in COVID-19, potentially informing diagnostic or therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways in stroke patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=6 per group) and exploratory design limit generalizability and causal inference. The study relies on thrombi retrieved during a specific pandemic wave, which may not represent later variants or broader populations, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory study investigated prothrombotic alterations in cerebral thrombi from COVID-19 stroke patients compared to non-COVID-19 controls during the first pandemic wave. Using histological, ultrastructural, proteomic, and elemental analyses, the authors identified increased cell-free hemoglobin and iron levels in COVID-19 thrombi, alongside reduced platelet content and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics revealed upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, and redox-regulating proteins, with downregulation of platelet-related proteins. These findings support a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability distinct from NETs or erythrocyte abundance. While the study provides mechanistic insights, its small sample size and focus on early pandemic thrombi limit generalizability and preclude causal conclusions.

title: Engineering antigenic breadth against SARS-CoV-2 by pairing divergent RBDs within a single mRNA immunogen.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are a major goal for pandemic preparedness, yet a challenge across vaccine fields is how to deliberately recruit the rare B cell clones that recognize conserved epitopes shared across diverse viral variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed an mRNA vaccine in which two antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variant receptor binding domains (Omicron and Delta) are physically fused on a single polypeptide, with a matched nondivergent tandem RBD (Delta-Delta) serving as a control.
analysis.methods: Using multicolor RBD tetramers and single-cell B cell receptor sequencing, the authors assessed B cell receptor selection and cross-reactivity pathways induced by the divergent and matched control vaccines.
analysis.main_results: In mice, immunization with the divergent vaccine elicited potent antibody responses and increased the frequency of cross-reactive B cells recognizing Delta, Omicron, and the 2002 pandemic strain SARS-CoV RBDs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The divergent vaccine preferentially enriches clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells with low somatic hypermutation, consistent with selection of germline-biased precursors, whereas the matched control yields cross-reactivity primarily through affinity maturation within existing clonal lineages.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work establishes a modular antigen-design principle in which juxtaposing appropriately divergent antigens on a single scaffold promotes the enrichment of bnAb-prone B cells, offering a strategy for broader vaccine coverage against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to preclinical mouse data and does not report human immunogenicity, durability of responses, or clinical efficacy, warranting cautious interpretation of translational potential.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) against diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants by designing an mRNA immunogen that pairs divergent receptor binding domains (RBDs) from Omicron and Delta on a single polypeptide. In mice, the divergent vaccine elicited potent antibody responses and increased cross-reactive B cell frequencies against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the 2002 SARS-CoV strain. Mechanistically, breadth arose via two pathways: the divergent vaccine enriched germline-biased, clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells with low somatic hypermutation, while the matched control vaccine induced cross-reactivity primarily through affinity maturation within existing clonal lineages. The authors propose a modular antigen-design principle to deliberately recruit bnAb-prone B cells, offering a potential strategy for broader vaccine coverage. However, the evidence is preclinical and limited to mouse models, leaving human immunogenicity, durability, and clinical efficacy unassessed.

title: Molecular Epidemiology of Emerging Subvariants of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Lineage: A Cross-sectional Study from Himachal Pradesh, India

analysis.research_question_and_background: Continuous genetic variation in SARS-CoV-2 drives the emergence of new lineages with potential impacts on transmissibility, pathogenicity, and immune escape, creating a need to monitor circulating variants for public health planning. The study aimed to detect the emergence of Omicron lineage subvariants in Himachal Pradesh, India, addressing gaps in local genomic surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Medical College, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, India, from January 2024 to June 2024. All SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct value ≤30 received from the state’s four Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories were included.
analysis.methods: RNA extraction was performed using the Q-Line Molecular Viral RNA Extraction Kit, and whole genome sequencing was carried out on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform. Consensus sequences were generated using Medaka and Nanopolish for variant identification and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.main_results: A total of 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were received, with adult females comprising 56.7% (17/30) and most patients aged 19–60 years (56.7%, 17/30). Samples were predominantly from Shimla (36.7%, 11/30), and JN.1 sublineages were identified in 63.3% (19/30) of cases. Most cases (66.7%, 20/30) presented to outpatient departments, with mild symptoms such as fever and cough in 35% (7/20). Although 76.7% (23/30) were vaccinated, 33.3% (10/30) required admission, and no mortality was reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The predominance of the JN.1 sublineage among sequenced cases indicates ongoing local circulation of Omicron subvariants with generally mild clinical presentation. The study highlights the utility of genomic surveillance in detecting emerging variants within a regional setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the integration of genomic surveillance with epidemiological data to enable early detection of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants and strengthen local control strategies in hilly regions. The predominance of JN.1 underscores the need for targeted public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=30) and single-centre design limit generalisability, and reliance on Ct ≤30 may introduce selection bias. The evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and lack of controls for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study from Himachal Pradesh, India, conducted between January and June 2024, investigated the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants through genomic surveillance. Among 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct ≤30, adult females and individuals aged 19–60 years were most represented, with samples predominantly from Shimla. Whole genome sequencing on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform identified JN.1 sublineages in 63.3% of cases, with most patients presenting mild symptoms and 66.7% managed as outpatients. Vaccination coverage was high (76.7%), yet 33.3% required admission, and no mortality was observed. The predominance of JN.1 highlights ongoing local circulation of Omicron subvariants with generally mild clinical outcomes. The study underscores the importance of integrating genomic surveillance with epidemiological data to detect emerging variants and inform public health strategies in hilly regions.

title: The Role of Community Health Workers in Increasing Access to Essential Health and Social Services During the COVID-19 Pandemic.

analysis.scope_and_question: To describe the health care and social services needs addressed by community health workers (CHWs) through referrals in the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We performed a descriptive analysis of national performance measure data from 67 CCR recipients from 2021 to 2024 documenting referrals, alongside 2 web-based surveys of 63 program administrators and 689 CHWs in the United States in early 2024.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CHWs made 464 158 social and 323 769 health referrals, with 282 596 referrals completed. CHWs connect individuals to health care and provide follow-up care and social support. Comprehensive and coordinated health and social services are essential to optimize the referral and service delivery.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Referral success was aided by community resources, CHW knowledge, and networking, and limited by costs, mistrust, language barriers, transportation, and child care challenges.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Findings support policies promoting the integration, expansion, and sustainability of the CHW workforce.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the role of community health workers (CHWs) in addressing health and social service needs during the COVID-19 pandemic through the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. The analysis combines national performance measure data from 67 CCR recipients (2021–2024) with web-based surveys of 63 program administrators and 689 CHWs in the United States. CHWs made 464,158 social and 323,769 health referrals, with 282,596 completed. Referral success was influenced by community resources, CHW knowledge, and networking, but constrained by costs, mistrust, language barriers, transportation, and child care challenges. The review highlights the importance of CHWs in connecting individuals to health care and providing follow-up support, emphasizing the need for comprehensive and coordinated services. Findings advocate for policies that integrate, expand, and sustain the CHW workforce to improve access to essential health and social services during public health crises.

title: The Impact of Setting Characteristics on Community Health Worker Roles and COVID-19 Activities: An Examination of the Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities Program.

analysis.scope_and_question: To examine the roles and activities performed by community health workers (CHWs) involved in the national Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program and examine differences based on setting characteristics.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We used data from a CHW self-report survey (n = 689) conducted February through March 2024 in the United States. We ran a series of ordered logistic regression models to examine the association between setting characteristics (i.e., type of organizational setting, organizational experience with CHWs, and populations of focus) and CHW core roles and COVID-19‒specific activities.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: A total of 69.2% of CHWs in the analytic sample reported performing all 10 core roles. Results suggest that CHWs in the CCR program tailored their roles and activities according to the unique factors of the communities in which they worked. Organizational experience with CHWs and populations of focus emerged as the most salient predictors of CHW core roles and activities.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report controversies or evidence gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the roles and activities of community health workers (CHWs) in the Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program, focusing on how setting characteristics influence their functions. The study used data from a self-report survey of 689 CHWs conducted in the United States between February and March 2024. Ordered logistic regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between organizational settings, experience with CHWs, and populations of focus with CHW roles and activities. The findings indicate that 69.2% of CHWs performed all 10 core roles, and their activities were tailored to the unique factors of their communities. Organizational experience and population focus were identified as the most significant predictors of CHW roles and activities. The study highlights the importance of context-specific approaches in CHW programs and suggests implications for public health strategies.

title: Evaluating the Potential Influence of Federal COVID-19 Response Funding on the Building and Sustainability of the CHW Workforce.

analysis.scope_and_question: To describe the potential influence of Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) funding on community health worker (CHW) hiring, retention, and workforce sustainability.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A descriptive analysis of a cross-sectional, web-based survey of directors and coordinators of 63 CCR recipient organizations administered between February and March 2024 was conducted in the United States.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Survey questions assessed program funding sources, payment mechanisms for CHW services, and CHW hiring and retention. About 65% of CCR recipients relied solely on CCR funds, whereas others leveraged over $117 million in additional funding, mostly federal, to support CCR program implementation. Of 1359 CHW positions supported by CCR, respondents expected to maintain 749.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Recipients planned to use grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement as strategies for retention. The findings underscore the importance of long-term investment via diverse funding sources and building programmatic capacity to strengthen and sustain the CHW workforce.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Federal funding can contribute meaningfully to sustaining CHW employment across different settings, yet sustainability of this vital public health workforce is not assured. Public Health Implications.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the influence of federal funding on the sustainability of the community health worker (CHW) workforce in the context of the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. A cross-sectional survey of 63 CCR recipient organizations was conducted between February and March 2024, assessing funding sources, payment mechanisms, and CHW hiring and retention. The findings indicate that 65% of recipients relied solely on CCR funds, while others used additional federal funding. Of 1359 CHW positions, 749 were expected to be maintained. Retention strategies included grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement. The review highlights the need for long-term investment and programmatic capacity to ensure CHW workforce sustainability, though federal funding alone may not guarantee it.

title: A Community Health Worker-Led Model of Training and Technical Assistance to Support National Community Health Worker Program Implementation for COVID-19 Response: United States, 2021-2025.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the training and technical assistance (TTA) needs of community health worker (CHW) programs in the United States during the COVID-19 response, focusing on the implementation and reach of a national CHW-led TTA program to support these programs from 2021 to 2025.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review describes an online survey and interviews conducted from December 2021 through January 2022 to assess TTA needs among 67 CDC-funded CHW programs, using findings to inform TTA content and delivery. Participation data were collected from 2021 through 2025 to assess program reach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that health departments implementing CHW programs demonstrated substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA, with the program reaching all funded recipients and generating 8824 participant encounters, 54.7% of whom were CHWs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in TTA needs across regions, populations, or program types, nor does it address conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms related to CHW-led TTA effectiveness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review implies that policymakers should prioritize sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to support the implementation and long-term sustainability of CHW programs, particularly in funding, hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates a national community health worker (CHW)-led training and technical assistance (TTA) program designed to support U.S. CHW programs during the COVID-19 response (2021–2025). Using survey and interview data from December 2021–January 2022, the program identified hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning as key TTA priorities. Based on these findings, the program developed webinars, communities of practice, leadership training, and individualized TTA. By 2025, the program reached all funded recipients, generating 8824 participant encounters, with 54.7% involving CHWs. The review highlights substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA among health departments, underscoring the need for sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to ensure program implementation and long-term sustainability.

title: Cytokine-Driven Hyperinflammation in Long COVID: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, Complement Dysregulation, and Emerging Immunotherapies-A Narrative Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: Long COVID, also known as post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), is a multisystem condition characterized by persistent symptoms that continue beyond the acute phase of infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, cohort studies, mechanistic investigations, and clinical trials examining immune dysregulation, inflammatory biomarkers, complement pathways, and targeted therapies in long COVID.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Persistent elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-6, interleukin-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, and interleukin-17, together with activation of the alternative and lectin complement pathways, contributes to endothelial injury, microvascular thrombosis, neuroinflammation, fibrosis, and multisystem dysfunction.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Robust prospective studies and randomized clinical trials remain essential to validate these strategies and optimize long-term clinical outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Emerging biomarkers include inflammatory cytokines, complement proteins, endothelial activation markers, coagulation indices, and multi-omics signatures that may improve disease stratification and therapeutic monitoring. Integrating validated biomarkers with precision immunotherapeutic approaches may improve diagnosis, risk stratification, and individualized management.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the mechanisms of cytokine-driven hyperinflammation in Long COVID, focusing on persistent immune dysregulation, complement activation, and vascular injury. The review synthesizes evidence from studies published between 2020 and 2026, sourced from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar. It highlights the role of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6, interleukin-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, and interleukin-17, as well as the alternative and lectin complement pathways, in contributing to multisystem dysfunction. The review also identifies emerging biomarkers that may enhance disease stratification and therapeutic monitoring, and suggests that integrating these biomarkers with precision immunotherapies could improve diagnosis and management. However, the review emphasizes the need for robust prospective studies and randomized clinical trials to validate these strategies and optimize long-term outcomes.

title: US Public School Operations During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Scoping Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review addresses SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19 impacts on US K-12 public school operations during the first two years of the pandemic, focusing on the implementation and effects of interventions and policies used to operate schools while balancing health protection with continuity of education and nonacademic services. [A1][A2][A3][A4][A5].
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The authors conducted a scoping review of the literature on interventions and policies for operating US K-12 public schools during the first two years of the COVID-19 pandemic, using thematic analysis to characterize the included evidence.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature supports that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination interventions enabled schools to safely conduct in-person learning, indicating that suitable mitigation measures allowed safe public school operation during the pandemic.

analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The supplied evidence indicates that effective implementation of school mitigation measures during the COVID-19 pandemic required adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in, and that reopening or continuing remote learning during a public health emergency demands careful planning to safeguard health while ensuring equitable continuation of education and access to nonacademic services.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review examines how US K-12 public schools were operated during the first two years of the SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19 pandemic, a period that began with sudden closures and a shift to remote learning that disrupted education and access to nonacademic services. Through thematic analysis of the literature on interventions and policies, the authors identified that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination enabled schools to safely conduct in-person learning, demonstrating that suitable mitigation measures permitted continued public school operation. The review emphasizes that effective implementation of these measures depended on adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in, and it underscores the need for careful planning to balance health and safety with equitable educational continuity and access to nonacademic services during future public health emergencies. No specific evidence gaps, controversies or quantitative pooled estimates are reported in the supplied evidence.

title: The influence of hypoxia in predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction on admission in 2 centers in sub-Saharan Africa.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the influence of hypoxia on predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction upon admission, highlighting the need to understand how these factors interact in disease progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A two-center retrospective cohort study was conducted involving 359 COVID-19 patients aged 18 years or older, with a focus on those presenting with kidney dysfunction and hypoxia.
analysis.methods: The study used multivariate Cox regression models to evaluate the association between mortality, hypoxia, and kidney dysfunction, with a significance level set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: Overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, increasing to 59.7% in patients with both eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and hypoxia (p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the combination of kidney dysfunction and hypoxia significantly increases mortality risk, indicating a potential pattern of kidney-lung cross talk.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results emphasize the importance of incorporating KD and hypoxia into patient stratification strategies for improved risk assessment and management in sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong given the clear statistical associations observed.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the influence of hypoxia on predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction upon admission in two centers in sub-Saharan Africa. It found that overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, rising to 59.7% in patients with both kidney dysfunction and hypoxia. The results suggest a potential pattern of kidney-lung cross talk, highlighting the importance of incorporating these factors into patient stratification strategies for improved risk assessment and management. The study's retrospective design and potential for confounding factors limit its evidence strength, although the observed statistical associations are robust.

title: Immunological imprinting shapes the cross-reactive antibody responses to the KP.2 and LP.8.1 vaccine doses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immune responses following a single KP.2 vaccine dose. The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2.86 subvariant necessitated the 2024-2025 vaccine update to include KP.2 or related JN.1-lineage spike antigens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal cohort study was conducted on 21 individuals to assess antibody responses up to 6 months after receiving a KP.2 vaccine dose. The study focused on evaluating the immune response against the ancestral WA.1 strain and various Omicron subvariants.
analysis.methods: The study used a live virus neutralization assay to measure neutralizing titers. Power-law modeling was applied to estimate the half-lives of IgG responses specific to WA.1 and KP.2. Serum-depletion experiments were also conducted to determine cross-reactivity of vaccine-elicited antibodies.
analysis.main_results: KP.2 vaccination increased spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral WA.1 strain, as well as against the BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2 variants. Power-law modeling estimated half-lives for WA.1- and KP.2-specific IgG responses at 770 and 248 days, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that KP.2 vaccine-induced antibodies retained broad neutralizing activity against recently circulating Omicron subvariants, but reduced neutralizing activity against certain emerging variants indicates ongoing antigenic changes can impact vaccine effectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide insight into how current vaccines perform over time and highlight the need to track viral evolution and update vaccine antigens to maintain broad protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and death.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and the focus on a single vaccine dose. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a longitudinal cohort study and serum-depletion experiments, but the results are directly observed and reported.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immune response generated by a single dose of the KP.2 mRNA vaccine in a longitudinal cohort of 21 individuals. It evaluates the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immunity against the ancestral WA.1 strain and various Omicron subvariants, including BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2. The results show that KP.2 vaccination increases spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against these variants, with power-law modeling estimating half-lives for IgG responses at 770 and 248 days for WA.1 and KP.2, respectively. Serum-depletion experiments reveal that most antibodies are cross-reactive, and the study highlights the importance of monitoring viral evolution to maintain vaccine effectiveness. However, the study's small sample size and focus on a single dose limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate.

title: Editorial: The influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on the incidence of viral coinfection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID influence the incidence of viral coinfection, highlighting the need to understand the interplay between these conditions and other pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients, focusing on the immune response to SARS-CoV-2 and its variants, including non-structural proteins involved in viral replication and immune evasion.
analysis.methods: Machine learning analyses identified key biomarkers of COVID-19 severity, such as IL-18, CRP, and IL-6, while also examining TCR clonotype characteristics in long COVID patients to assess monocyte function and differentiation.
analysis.main_results: A significant proportion of TCRs targeted epitopes across the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including non-structural proteins, and the analysis suggested reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation, indicating potential immune exhaustion or immaturity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the complex relationship between T cell protective immunity, the viral replication cycle, and HLA type, which influence TCR affinity and clonotype formation in SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that understanding T cell responses and their modulation by viral factors and HLA types could inform strategies for improving immune responses and managing long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on hospitalized Omicron patients and the lack of long-term follow-up data, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial explores the influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on viral coinfection incidence. It highlights the need to understand how these conditions interact with other pathogens and affect immune responses. The study analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients, identifying key biomarkers and suggesting reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation. These findings emphasize the role of the viral replication cycle and HLA type in shaping TCR affinity and clonotype formation. The results have implications for improving immune responses and managing long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2, though the study's moderate evidence strength is limited by its focus on hospitalized patients and lack of long-term data.

title: Extracellular vesicles in COVID-19 and long COVID: Structural mediators of viral persistence and immune dysfunction.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) as structural mediators in SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID, focusing on their capacity to preserve viral protein integrity, propagate immune dysregulation, and contribute to chronic inflammation and vascular injury.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes current insights into EV-associated viral remnants and host-derived inflammatory cargo, emphasizing their structural and functional contributions to neuro-immune crosstalk and systemic inflammation in COVID-19 and long COVID.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Extracellular vesicles released during SARS-CoV-2 infection function as organized lipid nanostructures that preserve the native conformational integrity of viral proteins, including spike glycoprotein, thereby facilitating chronic signaling and systemic inflammation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that recent advancements in single-particle analytical techniques, such as cryo-electron tomography and atomic force microscopy, are overcoming prior limitations of bulk analysis, enabling visualization of EV heterogeneity and quantitative profiling of nanomechanical properties.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review evaluates the potential of EVs as precision biomarkers and bioengineered therapeutic platforms, stressing the need for standardized structural characterization to transition these nanovesicles from physiological mediators to clinical diagnostic and regenerative tools.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how extracellular vesicles (EVs) act as structured mediators in SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID, preserving viral protein integrity and driving chronic immune activation and vascular injury. It synthesizes evidence on EV-associated viral remnants and host inflammatory cargo, emphasizing their role in neuro-immune crosstalk. The review concludes that EVs, as organized lipid nanostructures, facilitate persistent systemic inflammation by maintaining viral protein conformation. It also notes that emerging single-particle techniques are addressing prior analytical limitations, enabling detailed EV profiling. Finally, it proposes EVs as candidates for precision biomarkers and therapeutic platforms, contingent on standardized structural characterization for clinical translation.

title: Preliminary miRNA profiling of plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of miRNA in the host response to SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly focusing on how different variants may affect molecular pathways, including epigenetic mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used high-throughput microarray technology to assess miRNA expression in plasma samples from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron, compared to healthy controls.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed high-throughput microarray technology to measure miRNA expression levels and analyzed miRNA-mRNA interactions to identify potential target genes.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 65 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed in both SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to healthy samples, and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity in patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that miRNA profiling could provide novel insights into the host's epigenetic response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, highlighting potential biomarkers for disease progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies targeting miRNA pathways in SARS-CoV-2 infections, offering potential for improved prognosis and treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on miRNA expression without detailed analysis of comorbidities or pathway cross-talk, and the evidence is based on a single study with a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated miRNA expression in plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron, compared to healthy controls. Using high-throughput microarray technology, the researchers identified 65 miRNAs that were differentially expressed in both variants and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity. The findings suggest that miRNA profiling could offer new insights into the host's epigenetic response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, potentially aiding in diagnosis and treatment. However, the study's results are limited by the absence of detailed analysis of comorbidities and pathway interactions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Changes in patient conceptualization of asthma and asthma self-management at key timepoints across the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how people with asthma conceptualized their condition and self-managed it during key stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, as the specific impacts of the pandemic on asthma patients were less certain.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was a retrospective cross-sectional qualitative study involving 20 participants with asthma, examining their experiences across pre-COVID, initial outbreak/lockdown, restrictions lifting, and key stages relevant to them, such as vaccination.
analysis.methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted at one timepoint, and data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify patterns in participants' experiences and conceptualizations of asthma and self-management during the pandemic.
analysis.main_results: Three themes emerged: 'Doing my own risk assessment,' 'Asthma from background to foreground,' and 'Place in society,' highlighting participants' active risk evaluation, heightened awareness of asthma as a pre-existing condition, and societal inclusion/exclusion based on safety concerns.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the pandemic significantly altered how asthma was perceived and managed, with participants adjusting their behaviors based on evolving risk assessments, as per the Transdiagnostic model.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform public health messaging and support systems for individuals with asthma during future public health emergencies, helping to address their unique needs and concerns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single timepoint data collection and reliance on self-reported experiences, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong given the thematic analysis of a representative sample of asthma patients.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study investigated how people with asthma conceptualized their condition and managed it during key stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. The research aimed to understand the impact of the pandemic on asthma patients, as the specific effects were uncertain. Using semi-structured interviews with 20 participants, the study identified three themes: active risk assessment, asthma becoming a more prominent concern, and societal inclusion/exclusion based on safety perceptions. The findings highlight how the pandemic influenced asthma management behaviors and mental health, aligning with the Transdiagnostic model. These insights can guide public health strategies for supporting asthma patients during future crises. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and single timepoint collection may limit the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

title: Refining the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response post-COVID-19.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response, specifically examining how these disciplines have studied human behaviour during the COVID-19 pandemic. The central question is about the breadth and depth of this role, particularly in understanding the variability of human responses to public health interventions. The topic boundary includes SARS-CoV-2, its variants, and related terms such as 'post-COVID condition' and 'long COVID'.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic review methods or meta-analysis. It draws on general observations and interpretations of studies conducted during the pandemic, focusing on the conceptual frameworks used to understand human behaviour. The review does not report specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that the focus on aligning human behaviour with public health recommendations during the pandemic was relatively narrow. It suggests that this approach may have overlooked the complexity of human decision-making, particularly in the context of uncertainty and varying risk perceptions. The authors argue that considering heterogeneous rationality among individuals can enhance understanding of pandemic-related behaviours.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the narrow focus on compliance with public health recommendations may have led to an oversimplified view of human behaviour. It also identifies a gap in understanding how people perceive and calibrate risks during pandemics, especially in the context of uncertainty and uneven risk distribution. These limitations suggest a need for more nuanced approaches in future research.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends expanding the scope of behavioural and social science research to include a broader range of human responses and decision-making processes. It emphasizes the importance of examining pandemic salience and risk calibration to improve future preparedness, decision-making, and trust in public health measures.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. It critiques the narrow focus on aligning human behaviour with public health recommendations and highlights the need for a more comprehensive understanding of risk perception and decision-making. The authors suggest that considering heterogeneous rationality among individuals can improve pandemic preparedness and response. They also identify gaps in current research and recommend future directions to enhance trust and adaptability in public health strategies.

title: Factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants, 2023-2025.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19 and influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. The central question is about factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants, 2023-2025.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review analyzed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Logistic regression was used to examine factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. The supplied evidence does not report specific findings on the effectiveness of vaccination programs or the impact of socioeconomic factors on vaccine uptake beyond lower educational attainment being associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants aged [≥]65 years during the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn-Winter campaigns. It highlights that motivations for influenza vaccination include belonging to a risk group and reducing influenza risk, while barriers include concerns about safety and adverse effects. The study found that individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination and vice versa. Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of receiving a COVID-19 vaccination. The review suggests that these findings may inform strategies to improve vaccination coverage in the population. However, other results were weaker or varied by season, indicating potential evidence gaps.

title: Estimation of serial intervals and time-varying reproduction numbers across SARS-CoV-2 variants in childcare clusters: symptom onset vs. reporting dates

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate differences in serial intervals (SI) and time-varying reproduction numbers (Rt) estimates based on symptom onset versus reporting dates in COVID-19 childcare clusters across SARS-CoV-2 variant periods. Respiratory virus transmission in childcare centers is facilitated by dense contact patterns, making accurate estimation of SI and Rt essential for outbreak management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Nationwide data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (January 2020–February 2022) were analyzed. Four genotype-confirmed clusters meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included: one Before Delta, two Delta, and one Omicron cluster, each comprising at least 50 epidemiologically linked cases.
analysis.methods: Serial intervals were fitted using gamma distributions. Time-varying Rt values were estimated using the EpiEstim package separately based on symptom onset and reporting dates.
analysis.main_results: Onset-based mean SI declined from 9.85 days (95% CI: 1.97–23.95) in the Before Delta period to 5.34 days (95% CI: 2.00–10.28) during Omicron. In contrast, reporting-based SI estimates were generally longer, reaching 8.87 days (95% CI: 0.71–27.08) during Omicron. Across all variant periods, reporting-based Rt estimates were consistently lower than onset-based estimates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The choice of temporal reference substantially affects SI and Rt estimation in childcare clusters. Reliance on reporting dates may underestimate real-time transmission intensity and distort epidemic risk assessment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems may improve the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design or analysis methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the differences in serial interval (SI) and time-varying reproduction number (Rt) estimates for SARS-CoV-2 in childcare clusters using symptom onset versus reporting dates. The research highlighted that SI estimates based on symptom onset decreased across SARS-CoV-2 variant periods, while reporting-based estimates remained longer. Similarly, Rt estimates using symptom onset were consistently higher than those using reporting dates. The authors concluded that the choice of temporal reference significantly impacts SI and Rt estimation, with reporting dates potentially underestimating transmission intensity and distorting risk assessments. They emphasized the importance of prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems to enhance the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk environments. The study was based on nationwide data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, covering January 2020 to February 2022, and included clusters from different variant periods. The findings suggest that using reporting dates alone may not provide reliable estimates for outbreak management, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of detailed limitations.

title: Prognostic impact of right ventricular dilatation and echocardiography use criteria in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The surge of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 [coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)] infection created unprecedented diagnostic and logistical pressures. Given the established potential for cardiac injury and the critical need to optimize scarce resources, establishing the clinical utility and prognostic value of transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) became imperative.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We performed a retrospective cohort study analyzing records from patients with confirmed COVID-19 who underwent TTE. Total 149 patients were analyzed. Median age was 66 years [interquartile range (IQR): 56-73], median hospital stay was 13 days (IQR: 6-23).
analysis.methods: Socio-demographic, biochemical, and echocardiographic parameters were collected. Mortality was the primary outcome. We assessed inter-observer agreement (Kappa statistic) for TTE indications (based on American College of Cardiology Foundation 2011 and American Society of Echocardiography 2020 guidelines) and the determination of clinical impact (a subsequent change in patient management).
analysis.main_results: Overall and intensive care unit mortality rates were 39.6% and 60%, respectively. Elevated biochemical markers (leukocytes, neutrophils, lactate dehydrogenase, and C-reactive protein) were associated with mortality. Crucially, right ventricular (RV) dilatation and/or strain (P = 0.008) was identified as the sole echocardiographic finding significantly predictive of mortality. Inter-observer agreement for classifying AUC was high (κ ≥ 0.798). Furthermore, TTE prompted a change in clinical management in 79.7% of the cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: RV pathology is a potent, quantifiable prognostic indicator. While AUC demonstrated high reliability, the significant and frequent changes in management suggest that the current guidelines may possess inherent limitations when addressing the unique, acute prognostic complexities of severe COVID-19 disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the importance of incorporating right ventricular assessment in the echocardiographic evaluation of hospitalized COVID-19 patients for improved risk stratification and clinical decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on retrospective data, which may introduce bias and limit the ability to establish causality. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the prognostic impact of right ventricular dilatation and echocardiography use criteria in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. It highlights that right ventricular pathology is a significant predictor of mortality, while also noting that current echocardiography guidelines may have limitations in managing the acute prognostic complexities of severe disease. The findings suggest that incorporating right ventricular assessment into echocardiographic protocols could improve risk stratification and clinical decision-making for hospitalized patients. However, the study's retrospective design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the evidence, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Inequalities in mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection for people with severe mental illness during and following vaccination roll-out in England: a retrospective, whole-country linked cohort study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: People with severe mental illness (SMI) had a higher risk of death following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with people without SMI during the COVID-19 pandemic peak. It is unclear whether this risk reduced in later stages after vaccination roll-out.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective, whole-country cohort study analyzed linked electronic health records for all people in England registered to primary care who were alive in November, 2019. The study population included people who had COVID-19 between Jan 31, 2020, and June 30, 2023, with information on deaths and vaccination.
analysis.methods: Data were extracted from the NHS England Secure Data Environment provided through the British Heart Foundation Data Science Centre CVD-COVID-UK-COVID-IMPACT Consortium linked datasets, which were curated to form a dataset in July, 2024. Cox regression was used to estimate differences in all-cause and COVID-19 mortality.
analysis.main_results: 13 463 945 people with COVID-19 were identified, of whom 160 190 (1·19%) had SMI. People with SMI had higher all-cause mortality than those without (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1·56, 95% CI 1·53-1·59). All-cause mortality risk in people with SMI was elevated in stage 1 (aHR 1·27, 95% CI 1·22-1·32), but larger in the stage 2 (aHR 1·56, 1·51-1·61) and stage 3 (aHR 1·55, 1·50-1·59).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Excess mortality in people with SMI persisted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. Higher COVID-19 mortality risk in people with SMI persisted but was partially attenuated by vaccination (aHR 1·25, 1·17-1·34).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Preventive public health and clinical strategies are needed to address excess mortality and lower vaccination rates among people with SMI. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to reduce mortality risk in this vulnerable group.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated inequalities in mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection among people with severe mental illness (SMI) during and after vaccination roll-out in England. Using whole-country linked electronic health records, the researchers found that people with SMI had higher all-cause mortality compared to those without SMI, with the risk being elevated in all pandemic stages. The risk was partially reduced by vaccination, but excess mortality persisted. The study highlights the need for targeted public health and clinical strategies to address the higher mortality risk in people with SMI. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and potential for unmeasured confounding.

title: Sources of Stress in Relation to Sleep Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from the National Couples' Health and Time Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married/cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed the National Couples' Health and Time Study, an online survey completed between 2020 and 2021, involving 3,642 individuals.
analysis.methods: Stressors were categorized into five domains, including overall health, job/income, and public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration were measured, and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using survey-weighted logistic regression models.
analysis.main_results: Among the participants, 46.6% were aged 35-50 years, and 44.1% were college graduates. The weighted prevalence of stress varied across racial and ethnic groups, with overall health stress being highest among Latino individuals (62.0%) and job/income stress highest among Black/African American individuals (64.3%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that overall health stress and job/income stress were associated with poorer sleep health among married and cohabiting individuals, highlighting the impact of these stressors on sleep outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions for stress management and sleep health promotion in vulnerable populations during public health crises.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and its focus on married/cohabitating individuals, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married and cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using data from the National Couples' Health and Time Study, stressors were categorized into five domains, including overall health, job/income, and public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration were measured, and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using survey-weighted logistic regression models. The results showed that overall health stress and job/income stress were linked to poorer sleep health, with notable differences across racial and ethnic groups. The authors concluded that these stressors significantly impacted sleep outcomes, suggesting the need for targeted interventions. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a specific population limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.scope_and_question: This qualitative study aimed to understand perceptions and factors influencing COVID-19 and influenza vaccination among Black and African American adults to inform interventions and outreach to prevent increased acuity of vaccination disparities.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Eighty-six Black and African Americans in Milwaukee, WI were purposively recruited to participate in in-depth interviews. The study used qualitative methods to explore vaccine perspectives, influences, and decision-making.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Our findings show that vaccine perspectives are shaped by a complex interplay of personal beliefs, experiences, cultural identity, and trust. Major Findings We identified two themes and five subthemes reflecting vaccine perspectives, influences, and decision-making.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights that mistrust surrounding the COVID-19 vaccine fueled hesitancy, and some participants held discordant beliefs surrounding vaccines and healthcare. The study does not report on the effectiveness of interventions to address these issues.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Public health strategies to improve vaccination rates should acknowledge mistrust, dispel myths and misinformation, and engage trusted communities and messengers across both healthcare and community settings.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explores the perceptions and factors influencing vaccination against COVID-19 and influenza among Black and African American adults in Milwaukee, WI. The research identifies two main themes and five subthemes, including prevention as a motivator, mistrust of the vaccine, and the influence of life experiences on vaccine perspectives. The study emphasizes the need for public health strategies that address mistrust and engage trusted communities to improve vaccination rates. The findings suggest that vaccine hesitancy is shaped by a complex interplay of personal beliefs, cultural identity, and trust in healthcare systems. The research highlights the importance of targeted outreach and community-based interventions to reduce disparities in vaccination uptake.

title: Data-Driven Change-Point SEIR Modeling of the 2025 COVID-19 Epidemic Wave in China: Model Comparison, Robustness Analysis, and Residual Diagnostics

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to determine whether the 2025 epidemic wave of COVID-19 in China could be adequately modeled by a standard SEIR model with a constant transmission rate or if a structural change in transmission intensity was supported by the data.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 153 consecutive days of nationally reported COVID-19 cases from 1 May through 30 September 2025, using daily observations digitized from official China CDC figures and calibrated to monthly totals.
analysis.methods: A standard SEIR model was fitted under two specifications: a constant-beta baseline and a piecewise-beta model with a change point selected by profiling candidate dates and minimizing the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). Model performance was assessed using R-squared, RMSE, AIC, and BIC, with robustness evaluated through change-point, observation-scale, and biological-parameter sensitivity analyses, followed by residual diagnostics for day-of-week structure and temporal autocorrelation.
analysis.main_results: The AIC profile selected 24 May 2025 as the optimal change point, two days before the observed case peak on 26 May. The piecewise model substantially outperformed the constant-beta model (R-squared 0.8690 vs. 0.6689; RMSE 1,861.07 vs. 2,959.03; AIC 2,313.85 vs. 2,451.74; BIC 2,329.00 vs. The model-implied reproduction index declined from 1.4006 before the change point to 0.8725 afterward.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that a data-driven piecewise transmission rate provided a markedly better description of the 2025 epidemic wave than a constant-rate SEIR model, indicating a robust structural transition in transmission dynamics in late May.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that modeling transmission dynamics with a change point can improve the accuracy of epidemic wave predictions, which has implications for public health surveillance and response strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on nationally reported data and the potential for goodness of fit to deteriorate under some extreme biological assumptions. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the abstract-only nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the 2025 epidemic wave of COVID-19 in China using a data-driven SEIR model with a piecewise transmission rate. The analysis showed that the piecewise model outperformed the constant-rate model in terms of R-squared, RMSE, AIC, and BIC, indicating a structural change in transmission dynamics around late May. The model implied a decline in the reproduction index from 1.4006 to 0.8725 after the change point. The results suggest that incorporating change points in transmission rate modeling can enhance the accuracy of epidemic wave predictions. However, the study is limited by its abstract-only nature and potential for goodness of fit to vary under extreme assumptions, resulting in moderate evidence strength.
